pr_title: Disable build of HWAES on PPC Macs
pr_comments: Shouldn't it just move to the AESASM_ppc64?

> Shouldn't it just move to the AESASM_ppc64?

No because
1. aesp8-ppc.pl can be used on 32 bit ppc builds if the assembler understands the instructions and the CPU is detected to support Power ISA 2.07 
2. aesp8-ppc.pl now cannot be used on 64 bit ppc builds if the assembler does not understand the vpermxor instructions
Does this disable assembler that was previously used on those platforms?

> Does this disable assembler that was previously used on those platforms?

I do not think so - at least for Macs. The assembler was compiled in but it was never invoked anyway AFAIK.

AIX might be a different story - I am just replicating what we had to do with ChaCha20.

This brings up something interesting... will support for PPC OS X be dropped at any point in the near future? Apple has already dropped PPC support as of OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard). OS X 10.5.8 was the last version to support PPC, and that was released 2009-08-13. (Snow Leopard 10.6 did support 32-bit PPC apps via Rosetta, 10.6.8 was released 2011-07-25.)

So my understanding of the issue is:
- Some assemblers don't understand the instructions. We can either convert it to opcodes ourself, or just not build it for some platforms.
- The code would only be used on CPUs that support it, including a 32 bit build for 64 bit CPUs.
- At least the Mac never supported on a CPU that can make use of this

So I think for AIX, we have 2 options:
- Don't build it
- Convert it ourself

I think we've done both things in the past. It might be useful to have some kind of policy for this.

I think that if we decide to go with disabling things on a platform that can support it, we should at least document so.

This is a quick fix for the regression. We would need a proper community maintainer for AIX platform to do any better fix there. I suggest we merge this as is. Or alternatively I drop AIX from this patch as we did not get any bug report from AIX users yet, although I highly suspect we will get them later.
This pull request is ready to merge

> This brings up something interesting... will support for PPC OS X be dropped at any point in the near future? Apple has already dropped PPC support as of OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard). OS X 10.5.8 was the last version to support PPC, and that was released 2009-08-13. (Snow Leopard 10.6 did support 32-bit PPC apps via Rosetta, 10.6.8 was released 2011-07-25.)

For the record, this is not strictly accurate. While 10.6.8 only supports `ppc` via Rosetta, there are early versions of 10.6 running natively on PowerPC – in fact, that is my main testing system.

> @t8m I am sorry, perhaps I miss something, but the header seems not to have `ppc64` case at all, how is it supposed to work? Without `__ppc64__` it gonna be omitted on Darwin when building for ppc64.
> 
> I refer to this:
> 
> https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/b062a3c552bf283319dede3437598f1747730053/include/crypto/aes_platform.h#L63

Hmm... that is interesting. Not sure if this ever worked properly. However this is a separate issue. If you want to, please report a new issue. We would need someone to verify that it actually builds and works correctly on 64 bit PPC builds and it would be a master branch only fix.

> Could you advise how to test that locally?

You would have to set a breakpoint to that code (or patch it so it aborts) to see if it was invoked.

> > Could you advise how to test that locally?
> 
> You would have to set a breakpoint to that code (or patch it so it aborts) to see if it was invoked.

And what will be a test case where it should get invoked if working? Or just running make test?
Running `util/shlib_wrap.sh test/evp_test test/recipes/30-test_evp_data/evpciph_aes_common.txt` should invoke enough AES to see whether it calls this assembler code or not.
Merged to the master and 3.2 branches. Thank you for the reviews.
@t8m Sorry, I did not give up on checking assembler, I just had no time to deal with this yesterday. I will return to the matter shortly.

comments: @dannytsen Could you please look at this? Otherwise we will have to revert https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/21812
Hi @t8m , these instructions are 64 bits so it won't run on 32 bits.  This will run on p8 machine.  Did not expect it runs on 32 bits.  Thanks.
@dannytsen But previously that file was compilable and runnable on 32 bit. If you look at the build.info it is built on ppc32. We will have to revert this.

> @dannytsen But previously that file was compilable and runnable on 32 bit. If you look at the build.info it is built on ppc32. We will have to revert this.

Understand.

Same issue on AmigaOS, by the way.

However, I'm not so sure a revert is required here. I don't think `crypto/aes/aesp8-ppc.s` should ever be compiled for 32 bit targets anyway, before or now. They're not going to use it. So, it may be better to tweak `crypto/aes/build.info` in a similar way to the other p8-ppc modules for chacha and sha, for example.

My G5 is currently running Tiger (darwin 8), I should also check with Leopard (darwin 9) to see if OpenSSL 3.2 still chokes. It definitely does on Tiger but OpenSSL was previously built with no-asm and I don't recall why.

@Futaura Something like? (untested)
```
  $AESASM_ppc32=aes_core.c aes_cbc.c aes-ppc.s vpaes-ppc.s
  $AESDEF_ppc32=AES_ASM VPAES_ASM
  $AESASM_ppc64=$AESASM_ppc32 aesp8-ppc.s
  $AESDEF_ppc64=$AESDEF_ppc32
```

Maybe - not really sure if that will cover all cases. I was thinking something similar to this, for consistency:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/a435d786046fabc85acdb89cbf47f154a09796e1/crypto/chacha/build.info#L17-L21

That said, perhaps all the PPC conditional stuff needs cleaning up.

Correct me if I'm wrong, but with POWER8, for example, it can run in 32 or 64 mode? The asm modules appear to indicate that, so you can't put `aesp8-ppc.s` only in `$AESASM_ppc64`. So, it's more an issue that old compilers do not understand these newer instructions, hence the AIX and MACOSX check instead. There are certainly no PowerMacs that are capable of running the P8 or higher asm modules, obviously (same is true for AmigaOS).

Moved `aesp8-ppc.s` to `$AESASM_ppc64` in `crypto/aes/build.info` and tried to build with the `darwin-ppc-cc` & `darwin64-ppc-cc` on G5 running Tiger with GCC 4.0  & 4.2, it still failed. Will try on a G5 with Leopard over the next couple of days.

The assembly that gets generated targets the 970, so it should be runnable on a G5
I see `.machine        ppc970-64` in `aesp8-ppc.s`

The source code states:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/01d5e2318405362b4de5e670c90d9b40a351d053/crypto/aes/asm/aesp8-ppc.pl#L17-L18

So, although the code gets generated for all PPC builds (even in OpenSSL 3.1), even if it successful compiles, it will crash when you try to run it on a G5. I believe the CPU detection code stops this from happening, of course. It's just that the code used to compile with OpenSSL 3.1, but doesn't in 3.2 - the code was always linked in, even though it was never used.

review_comments: IIRC some Darwin systems were 64 bit PPC.  Is this going to disable the asm support for those platforms?  Or is that acceptable here?
No, it won't disable the asm support for AES completely. It's just the PowerISA 2.07 code that won't be built. And AFAIK it was not used anyway.
PowerISA 2.07 code won't be built for 32-bit and 64-bit; so _that_ code is gone from OS X regardless of whether its supported (i.e. on 32-bit)?
@tmshort AFAIK it was never supported by the CPUs used on Macs? Its just that the assembler previously built but it was not used anyway.
It seems that G5 was the only 64 ppc Mac, and didn't support that ISA.
G5 is ISA 2.02 with some extensions, AFAIK. Anything above ISA 2.03 is off question for sure.
